step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes MakeMyTrip's next-gen SOC system. Data is ingested from hybrid sources: AWS cloud services and on-premise data centers. This raw data flows into Apache Metron for parsing, enrichment, and profiling. A security data lake, consisting of EMR, S3, and Athena, stores historical telemetry events. EMR jobs transform data from Metron's persistent storage (HDFS) into S3. Athena is used for querying and analytics on this data lake. A critical feedback loop exists from the security data lake (S3) back to Apache Metron to enhance profiling and model generation. Apache Metron also sends alerts to a SOAR platform, which then orchestrates incident response, notifies SOC analysts, and triggers mitigation actions on services like WAF. The graph visually represents these data flows and components, with the transcript providing context on the purpose and specific interactions.

graph.name: MakeMyTrip Next-Gen SOC Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture for MakeMyTrip's next-generation Security Operations Center (SOC) system, built to detect and respond to advanced attacks using abnormal behavior detection. It integrates hybrid data sources, leverages Apache Metron for real-time processing, a serverless security data lake for long-term storage and analytics, and a SOAR platform for automated incident response.

nodes.name: AWS Log Sources
nodes.notes: Represents various AWS services (e.g., S3, SNS, SQS, CloudTrail, GuardDuty) generating telemetry events which are pulled into the SOC system. Treated as an external log source for this architecture.

nodes.name: On-Premise Data Center
nodes.notes: Represents on-premise log sources integrated via standard syslog or Kafka into the SOC system.

nodes.name: Apache Metron
nodes.notes: The heart of the next-gen SOC, responsible for data ingest, parsing, enrichment (adding contextual intelligence like geolocation, AS numbers), and profiling telemetry events in real-time. It also generates alerts.

nodes.name: Amazon EMR
nodes.notes: Used to pick up persistent data from Apache Metron's HDFS backbone and transform it for storage in Amazon S3 as part of the Security Data Lake.

nodes.name: Amazon S3
nodes.notes: The primary storage for the serverless Security Data Lake, housing telemetry events indexed over a long period (months to years). Enables large-scale, horizontally scalable storage for security forensics and analytics.

nodes.name: Amazon Athena
nodes.notes: Leveraged to build SQL queries and perform analytics, log mining, and forensics on the telemetry data stored in Amazon S3.

nodes.name: SOAR Platform
nodes.notes: A Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response platform (internally called 'Blitz'). It receives alerts from Apache Metron, enriches them with further contextual information, presents them to SOC analysts, and orchestrates automated or semi-automated responses.

nodes.name: SOC Analysts/Alerts
nodes.notes: Represents the human SOC analysts who receive alerts from the SOAR platform (e.g., via mobile or Jira integration) and interact with the system to investigate and respond to incidents. This node also encapsulates the alerting mechanism itself.

nodes.name: AWS WAF
nodes.notes: A target for mitigation actions from the SOAR platform, allowing analysts to block malicious sources or implement other security controls at the edge.

edges.notes: Telemetry events and logs from various AWS services (S3, SNS, SQS, CloudTrail, GuardDuty) are ingested into Apache Metron.
Syslog or Kafka integrated telemetry events from on-premise data centers are ingested into Apache Metron.
Persistent data from Apache Metron's HDFS backbone is picked up by an EMR job for further processing.
EMR transforms and stores the processed telemetry data into Amazon S3, forming the Security Data Lake.
Amazon Athena leverages data in S3 to build SQL queries, perform analytics, log mining, and forensics.
Feedback loop: Security Data Lake (S3) provides long-term telemetry information to Apache Metron for generating more accurate profiles and models, enhancing real-time enrichment.
Alerts generated by Apache Metron (after parsing, enrichment, and profiling) are fed into the SOAR platform for incident response.
The SOAR platform presents enriched alerts and incident details to SOC analysts (e.g., via mobile or Jira integration) for investigation and triage.
The SOAR platform triggers automated or semi-automated mitigation actions (e.g., blocking source IPs) on AWS WAF in response to detected threats.
